reason: Verified; the no-change verdict stands. (2) P(ABOVE THE x138 BLOCK): with L modelled correctly as the lowrefine effect (~1e-5 with a coin-flip sign, F-MOD-17; P(L<=0) 0.4-0.5), my 2M-draw MC (scratchpad r15_rcc_skeptic2.py) gives 0.92-0.94 for {#37,#38} and 0.84-0.89 for {#37,exp70d} when I~N(0.7e-3,0.7e-3). With I~N(0.4e-3,1e-3) it gives 0.83-0.86 against 0.66-0.76. exp70d can win this metric only if P(D > -I | I<0) > P(L>0) ~0.5-0.6, which needs mean D > ~0. That is implausible after the public read of -0.005. If L is wrongly given a 1e-3 spread, the ranking flips (r15_rcc_skeptic.py), so the claim depends on F-MOD-17, and F-MOD-17 holds. (3) UTILITY CHOICE CONFIRMED: there are ~3,94x teams, so bronze (top 10%, ~#394) falls inside the 0.953 x138 block (#342-723, 382 teams at 05:31Z). A tie sorts our late submissions to the end of the block. P(above block) is therefore close to P(medal). (4) RULES: exp70d is NEG under L5v2 (display 0.949). L9 admits a knob variant only at a display >= 0.955, and the R12-A3 table has no row for a NEG file. A swap would be post-hoc and would need a re-tick, so no-change is required by the rules regardless of the MC. OMISSION in the record, a caveat that does not refute it: the finding covers only the mean and the block. It leaves out the upper tail. With a wide sigma_D (0.003-0.004) and mean D between -0.001 and -0.002, P(max > +0.002 above x138) is 0.17-0.25 for {#37,exp70d} against 0.03. A linear rank utility then favours exp70d (444 vs 396). So exp70d buys a silver-tail chance for ~0.04-0.10 of medal probability. At the evidence-weighted centre (mean D ~ -0.0035, sd 0.002; the public embryo is the only test-domain read and the lab sign was wrong) that tail advantage disappears (0.04 vs 0.03), and {#37,#38} wins on every metric. No feasibility issue: no build, no submit, no rule change.
